All Streams prints 11 'already including Charge', and the disclosure says it reads Charge at one point per two Charge, so its 11 is what 12 Charge buys; Fathom the Tide spends 6 of that Charge for its extra 6. Cast All Streams while Charge is still 12 and it is worth 11; cast it after Fathom and it is reading only 6 Charge, so it would be worth about 8. Played in this order I deal 11 + 13 = 24 and leave Nibbit at 16 with 6 Charge banked. Reversed it is 21. I eat the full 12, going to 36/70, which is never close to dangerous.
answers.q2_other_line_considered: Two. The first was Fathom the Tide plus Coral Guard: 13 damage and 5 Block, so 7 through to face and Nibbit at 27. I rejected it because 5 Block against a 12 intent is not a wall, it is a discount, and buying 7 HP off a 48 HP pool with a card slot that could have been 11 damage is the wrong trade when nothing about this board threatens to kill me. The second was the Charge-conserving line, All Streams plus Water's Edge for 17, which leaves all 12 Charge intact so a future Fathom still has its full spend and All Streams keeps reading 11. That one I weighed properly, since Charge is a real resource and spending it now makes Fathom worse later, but 17 versus 24 is seven damage for a bank I have no printed reason to believe I need — nothing on this page tells me what a later turn looks like, and 24 now is the read I can actually justify from what is in front of me.
answers.q3_what_it_gave_up: The 5 Block, so I take the attack whole: 12 to the face rather than 7. It gave up half the Charge pool — 12 down to 6 — which makes the next All Streams read 6 Charge instead of 12 and leaves Fathom's spend clause exactly on the line at 6. And it gave up Water's Edge and Coral Guard entirely, both unplayed at 2 energy. In exchange, Nibbit ends at 16, which is inside one more turn's reach.
answers.q4_different_intent: Yes. The intent is what makes Coral Guard a rounding error here. At 12 incoming against 48 HP I can simply absorb it, so blocking buys nothing I need. Push the telegraph high enough that the hit threatens me — or start me low enough that 12 is a meaningful fraction of what is left — and Coral Guard stops being a wasted slot and starts being the card that keeps me alive to spend the banked Charge. A defensive or buffing telegraph would push the other way and make me even more comfortable dumping everything into damage. There is also a specific number that would flip the whole line: if Nibbit were low enough that 24 killed it, or if some line reached lethal that this one does not, the order and the card choice would be dictated by exact lethal instead of by max damage, and the Charge question would stop mattering at all.

line: All Streams Flow to the Sea

answers.q1_what_did_you_play: I spent both energy on damage: All Streams Flow to the Sea into Nibbit for 9 (Charge already counted), then Water's Edge for 6, for 15 total. That leaves Nibbit at 19/42 and I eat the full 12, going to 36/70. The reasoning is the clock. Nibbit is a single enemy at 34 HP hitting for 12 a turn; at roughly 15 damage a turn I need three attacking turns to kill it, and the enemy only gets to swing on the first two of those. That is 24 incoming across the fight. Anything I spend on defense now does not shorten the fight, it just moves the same 34 HP further out and buys the enemy another swing to be paid for later. With 48 HP I can afford two hits comfortably, so the cheapest total-damage-taken plan is to spend everything on closing the gap. I put All Streams first purely because it is the bigger hit and I wanted it on the board before anything could change; the page gives me no reaction or ordering effect that makes the sequence matter.
answers.q2_other_line_considered: Gyorin Formation alone, and I weighed it seriously — it is the closest call on the page. Two energy for 10 Block plus 6 at the start of next turn is 16 block against a 12-damage telegraph, which is more raw value than 15 damage and would have left me at 46/70 with a head start on the following swing. I rejected it because it deals zero: the fight still needs 34 damage out of me, and a turn of pure defense just adds a turn in which Nibbit gets to attack. Tallying both lines out to the kill, the totals came out within a few HP of each other, and I took the aggressive one because it ends the fight sooner and does not depend on future draws cooperating. I also looked at the middle line, Coral Guard plus All Streams — 5 Block and 9 damage, take 7 — and dismissed it as the worst of both: not enough block to matter against a 12, and it throws away a third of my damage.
answers.q3_what_it_gave_up: It gave up all 16 points of blocking, including the 6 that would have carried into next turn, and it gave up the safe HP total: I am at 36 instead of 46, and after the next swing I will be at 24, which is where the fight starts to have a floor I care about. It also gave up flexibility — if my next hand is short on damage, the tempo I bought here is wasted and I will have taken 12 for nothing.
answers.q4_different_intent: Yes. Attack for 12 against 48 HP is exactly the band where racing is affordable; move the number and the answer moves. A substantially bigger hit — say high teens or more — makes Gyorin Formation correct, because 10 Block plus 6 next turn converts a threatening swing into a survivable one and my HP stops being a resource I can freely spend. A defensive or buffing intent, or any turn where Nibbit was not attacking at all, would have made the all-damage line strictly free rather than a trade, and I would have played it with no deliberation. A telegraph of a multi-hit attack would also have changed it, since 10 Block absorbs a big single hit far better than several small ones and I would have had to re-weigh Coral Guard.

Trading 12 HP for 6 extra damage against an enemy still at 34 is a bad rate this early in the fight, so it lost. Second, Gyorin Formation alone: 10 Block now and 6 more at the start of next turn, which is 16 Block across two turns for 2 energy versus Twin Tides' 12. But it leaks 2 damage this turn and deals nothing, and its 10 is also charge-inflated, so it is buying next turn's defense at the price of this turn's tempo. Twin Tides plus an attack beat it on both axes that mattered.
answers.q3_what_it_gave_up: Charge, mainly. I burned 8 down to 2, which deflates All Streams Flow to the Sea and Gyorin Formation for the next few turns until it rebuilds — a copy of All Streams drawn next turn is a much smaller card than the one I just played. I also gave up the 6 Block that Gyorin would have deposited at the start of my next turn, so I enter that turn naked, and I gave up the 6 damage Water's Edge would have added, along with its Hydro application.
answers.q4_different_intent: Yes. The 12 is what made Twin Tides' expensive half worth the Charge — it is the exact number that makes 12 Block a full negation rather than an overpay. If Nibbit had telegraphed a small hit, a block, a buff, or anything non-damaging, I would have played Water's Edge and All Streams Flow to the Sea for 15 damage and kept all 8 Charge, since there would be nothing to defend against and Charge is worth more banked. If the intent had been much larger than 12, say 20-plus, Twin Tides would stop being a clean negation and I would have looked hard at Gyorin Formation instead, or just accepted the hit and pushed damage.

answers.q1_what_did_you_play: All three one-cost cards, spending exactly 3 energy: All Streams Flow to the Sea into Sludge Spinner for 9 (Charge already counted), Water's Edge into it for 6, then Coral Guard for 5 Block. That is 15 damage, taking the Spinner from 37 to 22, and the telegraphed 8-damage attack lands into 5 Block so I take 3 and end at 45/70. There is no lethal available this turn at any energy split, so the turn is about maximizing damage per energy while blunting a known hit, and the three cheap cards do both with nothing left over.
answers.q2_other_line_considered: Rally the Isles for 2, then one one-cost with the last energy. I weighed it as the setup line: Muster 2 turns two of the remaining hand cards into random Inazuma Companions and the +1 Charge nudges the Charge pool. Against a 37 HP enemy that will take roughly three turns to chew through, paying tempo for a possibly better hand is a real thought. I dropped it because Rally itself deals nothing and blocks nothing, it would cost me at least 6 known damage plus either the 5 Block or the other attack, the +1 Charge does nothing here since All Streams reads Charge at one point per two and 8 to 9 is not a step, and Muster's picks are the game's random roll, so I would be trading guaranteed value for an unknown against an enemy that is already hitting me.
answers.q3_what_it_gave_up: The Muster entirely. Two cards I would have transformed stay whatever they are, I do not see what companions the roll would have offered, and the Charge does not advance. If this fight runs long, the line I skipped is the one that could have compounded, and I spent the turn on flat rate instead. I also emptied my hand of all three cheap cards, so whatever I draw into next turn is unsupported by anything held back.
answers.q4_different_intent: Yes. If the Spinner had telegraphed nothing, a buff, or an attack small enough to shrug off, Coral Guard's 5 Block would be wasted and I would strongly consider Rally the Isles plus All Streams Flow to the Sea, taking the free window to Muster and set up rather than spending energy on unneeded Block. A much larger telegraphed hit would not have changed anything, since 5 Block plus two attacks is already the most I can do about it with this hand and I cannot outrace a 37 HP enemy by dropping the block.
